The property is verified when three things hold together. First, every frame in the sequence carries a signature that validates against the same declared public key, using the documented canonical byte encoding of the frame body, with no frame accepted on a relaxed or re-encoded form. Second, folding the verified frames in their declared order through the specified fold function, starting from the documented initial value, yields a final value that is byte-for-byte equal to the claimed value published alongside the sequence. Third, the fold is deterministic across implementations, meaning a second independent implementation reproduces the identical output from the identical inputs, which is the actual interop question. The check fails if any single frame fails signature validation, if reordering or dropping a frame still reaches the claimed value, which would show the fold is not binding, or if two conforming implementations disagree. To close this review, the submitter needs to provide the frame bytes, the public key, the fold definition, and the claimed value in one bundle so a reviewer can run the steps above and record the observed result.
